title: Number of Segments in a String
statement: Count how many segments the string `s` contains and return that count. A segment is a maximal run of consecutive characters none of which is a space. Spaces may appear anywhere, including at the start, at the end and several in a row, and an empty string or one made only of spaces has no segments.
constraints: s contains only English letters (lowercase and uppercase), digits, spaces and the characters !@#$%^&*()_+-=',.:
The only whitespace character in s is the space ' '

notes:
## Intuition

Every segment has exactly one first character, so counting segments is the same as counting the positions where a segment begins. A position begins a segment when it holds a non-space character and either sits at index 0 or comes right after a space. The quick alternative of splitting on `' '` works too, but it produces empty pieces for leading, trailing and repeated spaces that must be filtered out.

## Approach

1. Set `count` to 0.
2. Walk the string with index `i`.
3. Mark position `i` as a start (`isStart`) when `s[i]` is not a space and the character before it is a space or does not exist.
4. Add one to `count` for every start.
5. Return `count` after the scan.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "Hello, my name is John"`. Index 0 holds `H` with nothing before it, so `count` becomes 1. The letters `e`, `l`, `l`, `o`, `,` follow non-space characters and are skipped. Index 7 holds `m` after a space, so `count` is 2. In the same way `n` at index 10, `i` at index 15 and `J` at index 18 each follow a space and raise `count` to 3, 4 and 5. The scan ends and the answer is `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every character is checked once against itself and its left neighbour.
- Space: O(1): only a counter and an index.

## Pitfalls

- Counting spaces and adding one is wrong: it fails on `""`, on strings of only spaces and on repeated spaces.
- Splitting on `' '` without dropping empty pieces counts `"  a  "` as 5 instead of 1.
- Check `i === 0` before reading `s[i - 1]`; the first character can start a segment with no space before it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | number of segment starts seen so far |
| `i` | index of the character being checked |
| `isStart` | whether `s[i]` is the first character of a segment |

narration.2: No segments have been found yet.
narration.4: Look at every character of the string once, left to right.
narration.5: A segment starts here when this character is not a space and it is the first character or follows a space.
narration.6: Only the first character of each segment is counted.
narration.7: Found a new segment, so add one to the count.
narration.10: Each segment was counted exactly once at its start; return the total.
